issues.legal_issue: A challenge to land-acquisition notifications may be dismissed when it is brought after an unreasonable delay, particularly after the acquisition has substantially progressed on the basis of those notifications.
material_facts: The government initiated acquisition proceedings for planned urban development, issued and published an initial acquisition notification, later issued a declaration and notices to claimants, and made an award.
No objection was made during the statutory objection stage.
The challengers filed writ petitions about nine years after the declaration, challenging the acquisition notifications and later notices on grounds available when the notifications were published.
issues.conclusion: The High Court rightly dismissed the petitions for inordinate delay, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A challenge to an acquisition notification and declaration must be brought within a reasonable time. The length of delay matters in light of the acts done in the interval on the basis of the notification and declaration. Allowing the government to complete acquisition proceedings and then challenging instruments on grounds available when they were published would reward dilatory tactics. The Court followed Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi, [1975] 1 SCR 802, and referred to the acquisition sequence under sections 4, 5A, 6 and 9 of the Rajasthan Land Acquisition Act, 1953.

rule.if: acquisition_notification_challenge and unreasonable_delay_after_declaration and (acquisition_process_substantially_completed_before_challenge or government_acted_on_notifications_as_valid) and grounds_available_at_publication

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding seeks to invalidate notifications or declarations issued in a land-acquisition process.
predicates.unreasonable_delay_after_declaration: The challengers waited an unreasonable time after the acquisition declaration before bringing their challenge.
predicates.acquisition_process_substantially_comple: The government had substantially advanced the acquisition process before the challengers brought their case.
predicates.government_acted_on_notifications_as_val: The government proceeded with acquisition steps on the basis that the notifications and declaration were valid.
predicates.grounds_available_at_publication: The challengers relied on grounds that were available when the relevant notifications were published.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition challenge is brought unreasonably late after the declaration, the acquisition has meanwhile substantially advanced or the government has acted on the notifications as valid, and the grounds were available at publication, the challenge is dismissed for delay.
